source_title: Tata Punch launched in South Africa - Autocar India
source_excerpt:
Tata Motors has launched the Punch compact SUV in South Africa, with prices starting at R224,900 (approximately Rs 12.82 lakh). It is available in three trims, namely Pure+, Adventure and Accomplished+, with two engine options – a 1.2-litre naturally aspirated petrol and a 1.2-litre turbo-petrol – both paired with a manual gearbox. Unlike the India-spec model, the South African version does not get a CNG or an AMT option with the naturally aspirated engine. However, Tata is offering a longer warranty on the South African-spec model.
The Punch costs much more in South Africa than in India
South Africa-spec Tata Punch prices (in South African Rand)
The South Africa-spec Punch is priced from R224,900 to R269,900, which is approximately Rs 12.82 lakh to Rs 15.36 lakh. In comparison, the India-spec model costs between Rs 5.74 lakh and Rs 10.76 lakh. However, the price gap needs to be viewed in the context of export costs and market-specific taxes.
South Africa-spec Tata Punch vs Indian model: Key differences
Petrol AMT, CNG (MT and AMT) powertrains missing from South African line-up
As stated earlier, the South Africa-spec Tata Punch is offered with two engine options. One is a 1.2-litre three-cylinder naturally aspirated petrol mill producing 88hp and 115Nm, paired with a 5-speed manual gearbox. The other is a 1.2-litre three-cylinder turbo-petrol unit generating 120hp and 170Nm, paired with a 6-speed manual transmission.
In addition to these engine options, the India-spec model gets a CNG powertrain. Tata also offers an AMT option with the naturally aspirated petrol and CNG versions in our market.
Same exterior and interior design and features as the India-spec model
The South African-spec Tata Punch shares its exterior design with the India-spec model, including LED headlights with daytime running lamps (DRLs), a front grille, connected LED tail-lights and a rear skid plate. It also gets 16-inch alloy wheels, roof rails and identical bumpers.
The interior is the same as well, including the dashboard layout, a 10.25-inch touchscreen infotainment system, a 10.25-inch digital driver’s display and a two-spoke steering wheel. Feature highlights include automatic climate control with rear AC vents, a single-pane sunroof, wireless phone charging and ambient lighting. The safety equipment is also carried over, with six airbags as standard, electronic stability control, a 360-degree camera and a tyre pressure monitoring system.
However, the South African-spec Tata Punch gets a longer warranty than its Indian counterpart, with coverage of 5 years or 125,000km as against 3 years or 100,000km.
